# The Cell Table {#sec-cell-table}

Three binary axes — determination, certifiability, monotonicity — give
eight nominal combinations. Two of them are not merely unobserved; they
are **empty by theorem**: the determination gate (@sec-theorem) forces
any claim that fails determination to also fail every scheme regardless
of the other two axes, so a cell that would otherwise ask "not
determined, yet certifiable" cannot be inhabited by construction. The
table's empty cells are a corollary, not a gap in the search for
witnesses.

That leaves six inhabited cells: exactly one combination that passes all
three axes — the verifiable case the rest of this paper is implicitly
contrasted against — and five distinct ways to fail, each a distinct
flavor of trust with its own named witness claim and its own minimal
repair.

| Determined | Certifiable | Monotone | Status | Witness (illustrative) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | verifiable | inclusion in a canonical record |
| no | — | — | **empty by theorem** | (determination gate) |
| no | — | — | **empty by theorem** | (determination gate) |
| yes | yes | no | trust flavor | current-head / revocation claims |
| yes | no | yes | trust flavor | degeneracy of a forced generator (example-grade; full treatment is the follow-up build-domain paper) |
| yes | no | no | trust flavor | TODO — mixed witness pending |
| no | yes | — | trust flavor | genuineness / authorship claims |
| no | no | — | trust flavor | TODO — mixed witness pending |

Each of the five trust-flavor rows names a distinct minimal repair in
@sec-cures, not a single generic "trust more" — this table doubles as
the evidence for the claim in @sec-scope-objections that the floor does
not silently swallow every failure into one undifferentiated bucket.
